amendments.rule: A supplied English relative clause does not realize the article that governs it. Where the ASV renders an attributive participle as a finite clause — `τὴν δύναμιν τὴν ἐνεργουμένην` → *the power that worketh*, `τὸν καλούμενον` → *which is called* — the relativizer and any copula are helpers on the participle under rules 7 and 9, and the second attributive article stays its own `unrepresented` unit under rule 23. The test against rule 32 is whether the article governs an expressed head noun. `τῷ θεῷ τῷ κτίσαντι` → *God who created* has one, so the second article realizes nothing and *who* is the participle's helper; a bare `Τῷ δυναμένῳ` → *unto him that is able* has none, so the article is substantival and takes the pronoun itself. That test decides only the cases where a participle follows, because the participle is what carries the relativizer. Where the article's modifier carries **no verb of its own** — a **prepositional phrase**, or a bare **adverb** — there is nothing there to carry the relativizer, so the article keeps the supplied relativizer whether or not it governs an expressed head noun, and the copula goes with the preposition or with the adverb: `τὰ στρατεύματα τὰ ἐν τῷ οὐρανῷ` → *the armies which are in heaven* gives *which* to the second article and *are in* to `ἐν`, as `τὰ ἄνω` → *the things that are above* gives *the things that* to the article and *are above* to `ἄνω`. An adverb is no different from a prepositional phrase here, rule 53 already giving an adverbial predicate the supplied copula; and where the article is substantival it takes the supplied nominal along with the relativizer under rule 22, headed on the nominal word and never on the determiner or on the relativizer. Which side takes the English *the* is decided by where the article stands, not by the relative clause. An article that **follows** its noun leaves the determiner on the noun, supplying one there when the noun is anarthrous: `καρπὸν δικαιοσύνης τὸν διὰ Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ` → *the fruits of righteousness which are through Jesus Christ* gives *the fruits* to `καρπόν` and only *which* to `τόν`, as `κατὰ δικαιοσύνην τὴν ἐν νόμῳ` → *as touching the righteousness which is in the law* gives *the righteousness* to `δικαιοσύνην`. An article that **precedes** the noun it governs is that noun's own determiner and takes *the* along with the relativizer, headed on *the*, leaving the noun bare: `τὴν ἐκ θεοῦ δικαιοσύνην` → *the righteousness which is from God* gives the discontinuous *the … which* to `τήν` and *righteousness* to `δικαιοσύνην`, as `τὴν καθ' ὑμᾶς πίστιν` → *the faith … which is among you* does. That is rule 22's determiner clause holding where a head noun is expressed: the article carries the English determiner unless its own noun has already stood in front of it. An article left `unrepresented` in front of such a verbless modifier is right only where the ASV supplies no relative clause at all.
amendments.why: Rule 31's carve-out gives the article the supplied relativizer where its modifier has no verb to carry one, but names only a prepositional phrase. COL.3 met the same configuration with a bare adverb three times — `τὰ ἄνω` → *the things that are above* at 3:1 and 3:2, beside the prepositional `τὰ ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς` → *the things that are upon the earth* in the same verse — and the rule's own reason covers it: an adverb has no verb either. Rule 53 already gives an adverbial predicate the supplied copula and rule 84 records `ἔξω` → *without are* and `ἔξωθεν` → *without were*, so the copula side is corpus-attested and nothing here contradicts it. Returned as an amendment rather than a new rule because the over-broad word was the scope term 'prepositional phrase' itself; a cross-reference would have left a verse pass reading rule 31 first with no way to place an adverb, since rule 22 says nothing about relativizers and rule 32 speaks only of participles. The sentence about a substantival article taking the supplied nominal with the relativizer is added for the same reason: `τὰ ἄνω` combines rule 22's determiner clause with this carve-out, and the head belongs on the nominal word.

conventions: A supplied English verb resuming a Greek ellipsis is folded only where its own clause still has a token to carry it. 3:13's οὕτως καὶ ὑμεῖς expresses a subject and no predicate, so 'do' rides with ὑμεῖς under rule 56, which rule 62 has already freed from being a copula. 3:14 and 3:17 have no such token: every source token's English there is complete, and the licensing verb is spent — at 3:12 for 3:14's 'put on', at t004 for 3:17's 'do' — so the supplied verb is its own `added` unit under rules 5 and 103. An expressed object or adjunct is not a carrier: rule 62 wants a prepositional predicate, and ἐπὶ πᾶσιν τούτοις (3:14) and ἐν ὀνόματι (3:17) are adjuncts. The ASV's italics agree here but did not decide it (rule 11).

Where one English *-soever* word covers πᾶν ὅ τι ἐάν (3:17), the relative cluster takes it whole as one `aligned` unit under rules 50 and 72 and the quantifier πᾶν is left `unrepresented`, as ὃ ἐάν takes it at 3:23. Rule 80's opposite result is scoped to πᾶς governing a substantival article, which rule 32 limits to a pronoun and nothing else; a relative pronoun with its generalizing particle has its own claim on both halves of the word, 'what-' answering to the relative and '-soever' to the particle. Giving 'whatsoever' to πᾶν and emptying the other three tokens remains defensible and is how BSB reads it.

report: Checked all 31 candidate lemma groups and found no cross-verse split: every bucket with more than one treatment traces to a difference the source or the ASV's phrasing licenses. No patches.

ὁ (56 tokens, 13 treatments) is rules 19/21/23 operating on what the ASV wrote. Determiner written with an article present: the article takes it (3:23 'unto the', 3:24 'of the' and 'the'). Determiner written with anarthrous Greek: helper on the noun (3:17 'of the Lord', 3:18/3:20/3:24 'the Lord', 3:22 'the flesh'). No determiner written: article unrepresented and the case preposition stays with the noun (3:6, 3:15, 3:16, 3:17). The supplied possessive goes to the article where no genitive pronoun competes (3:5, 3:18, 3:19, 3:20) and the article is emptied where one does (3:3, 3:8, 3:9, 3:15, 3:16, 3:21); 3:22 is rule 76's availability arm, the article being already spent on 'them'. The vocative articles at 3:18-3:22 are all bare and all unrepresented (rule 89).

The two καί of 3:13 are decided by the English the ASV wrote, not by the Greek pairing: 'even' to the καί answering καθώς (rule 82's bare-even arm, καθώς keeping a bare 'as') and 'also' to the καί answering οὕτως (rule 100, οὕτως keeping 'so'). Support-verb frames divide by the object's case exactly as rules 21 and 106 require: 'on' stays inside φρονεῖτε (3:2) and 'for' inside κομίσεται (3:25) over accusatives, while the dative of ὑποτάσσεσθε (3:18) releases its 'to' to the article. Preverb particles ride inside their verb (3:1 'together', 3:8 'away', 3:9 'off', 3:10 and 3:12 'on') except at 3:16, where an expressed ἐν answers the preverb and keeps the word.

Read the dump end to end for the added-versus-folded asymmetry the table cannot see. Four added units: 3:14 'put on', 3:16 two list junctures (rule 98), 3:17 'do'. 3:13's supplied 'do' is folded onto ὑμεῖς while 3:17's is added, and the clauses differ: 3:13 expresses a subject and no predicate (rule 56, which rule 62 has already freed from being a copula), while 3:17's clause has an object and an adjunct whose English is complete and a verb already spent at t004 (rule 103). 3:14 is the same shape with the licensing imperative standing back at 3:12, and its note names that verse. Recorded as a convention.

BSB: five disagreements, none a genuine error. 3:4 ἡ and 3:12-shape possessives are rule 20; 3:6 τῆς and 3:16 τῷ are rules 21 and 23, the latter being rule 21's explicit refusal of a bare 'to' on an article the ASV gave no determiner; 3:10 τόν is rule 31's second attributive article. 3:17 πᾶν is the one genuinely contested edge — BSB's reading is the competing one the verse note already records — and I left the accepted edge alone; it is now in the conventions log.

One amendment, no new rule. Rule 31's carve-out is written for a prepositional-phrase modifier, and this chapter met a bare adverb three times (τὰ ἄνω → 'the things that are above' at 3:1 and 3:2). The rule's own reason — no verb to carry the relativizer — covers an adverb, and rule 53 with rule 84's ἔξω → 'without are' already puts the copula on an adverbial predicate, so the sentence is widened where it stands rather than qualified from a distance.
